nodes.summary: There exist an integer $k \ge 1$ and a finite multigraph (loops and parallel edges allowed) with at least two vertices, in which every partition of the vertices into two nonempty sets is crossed by at least $4k$ edges, such that no orientation of the edges makes the indegree minus the outdegree of every vertex divisible by $2k + 1$.
nodes.title: Jaeger's modular orientation conjecture is false

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every integer $k \ge 1$, every finite multigraph (loops and parallel edges allowed) that has at least two vertices, and in which every partition of the vertices into two nonempty sets is crossed by at least $4k$ edges, admits an orientation of its edges in which, at every vertex, the indegree minus the outdegree is divisible by $2k + 1$.
nodes.title: Jaeger's modular orientation conjecture

nodes.summary: Consider a multigraph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$ in which each edge has a first and a second endpoint. For a set $S \subseteq V$, an edge crosses the cut at $S$ when exactly one of its two endpoints lies in $S$.
nodes.title: Edges crossing a cut

nodes.summary: Consider a multigraph with finitely many edges in which each edge has a first and a second endpoint. For a set $S$ of vertices, the size of the cut at $S$ is the number of edges crossing it, that is, having exactly one endpoint in $S$. Distinct parallel edges are counted separately.
nodes.title: Size of a cut

nodes.summary: In a multigraph with finitely many edges and a chosen orientation, the indegree of a vertex $v$ is the number of edges whose head is $v$, parallel edges counted separately.
nodes.title: Indegree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a finite multigraph is $4k$-edge-connected when it has at least two vertices and, for every set $S$ of vertices such that both $S$ and its complement are nonempty, at least $4k$ edges cross the cut at $S$, that is, have exactly one endpoint in $S$. Parallel edges are counted separately. For $k \ge 1$ the condition implies that the multigraph is connected.
nodes.title: 4k-edge-connected multigraphs

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, an orientation of a multigraph with finitely many edges is a modulo $(2k+1)$ orientation when at every vertex the indegree minus the outdegree is congruent to $0$ modulo $2k + 1$.
nodes.title: Modular orientations

nodes.summary: Each edge $e$ of the multigraph has a reference direction from its first endpoint to its second endpoint, and an orientation chooses for each edge whether to reverse it. The head of $e$ is its second endpoint if $e$ is not reversed and its first endpoint if $e$ is reversed.
nodes.title: Head of an oriented edge

nodes.summary: Each edge $e$ of the multigraph has a reference direction from its first endpoint to its second endpoint, and an orientation chooses for each edge whether to reverse it. The tail of $e$ is its first endpoint if $e$ is not reversed and its second endpoint if $e$ is reversed.
nodes.title: Tail of an oriented edge

nodes.summary: In a multigraph with finitely many edges and a chosen orientation, the outdegree of a vertex $v$ is the number of edges whose tail is $v$, parallel edges counted separately.
nodes.title: Outdegree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
